title: Jump Game
description: Given nums where nums[i] is the max jump length from i, determine if you can reach the last index. Greedy: walk forward tracking the farthest reachable index.

notes: If i ever exceeds reach, you cannot have walked here — return false.
Once reach >= nums.length - 1 you could return true early, but the loop is fine.
Greedy beats DP here: you only need the farthest reachable, not per-index reachability.

options: The farthest index reachable from indices walked so far
Index of the last zero seen
It means no earlier index could jump to i, so the path is broken
JS arrays cannot be indexed past length

questions.q: Why is greedy correct here versus DP?
options: You only need the farthest reachable index — not whether each index is reachable individually
Greedy uses less memory by luck
questions.explain: If you can reach some j, you can reach every i < j. So one running max captures everything.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the greedy reachability check.

blanks.hint: the farthest reachable index so far
extend reach if i + nums[i] is larger
if we finished the loop without bailing

L3.prompt: Write `canJump(nums)` returning true iff you can reach the last index. Log `canJump([2,3,1,1,4])` then `canJump([3,2,1,0,4])`.
hints: Track the farthest index you can reach as you walk left to right.
If the loop index ever exceeds that farthest, you are stuck.
